transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-03
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Aerolith CTO), Ethan Wu (Aerolith Platform Eng), Sara Bloom (Aerolith Security), Liam (Product), Unidentified (Ops)

Summary (auto): Aerolith is planning to move off OpenAI due to pricing and control reasons; evaluating Redwood for a staged migration. They run a mixture of chat + embeddings + reranking workloads, heavy on short-turn latency for product features and some asynchronous batch jobs. Primary concerns: parity on quality with their current TGI/vLLM stack, predictable latency under peak, and encryption/KMS + audit requirements for regulated customers.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:12] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, with Diego, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:18] Priya Nair: Hey, doing good. We got a few people on the call, short agenda — why we're thinking about leaving OpenAI, what we run today, and what we'd need from Redwood to consider a move.
[00:00:27] Diego Alvarez: Cool, sounds good. Quick run through — Diego, SE, focusing on perf and compatibility. We'll ask a few questions about your traffic and then sketch hosting options.
[00:00:34] Ethan Wu: Quick heads up — we have a lot of short chat sessions, p95 latency under 300ms currently, and we do embeddings for semantic search at the index refresh cadence. We also have a couple of bulk reranker pipelines that run nightly.
[00:00:44] Sara Bloom: From security side, SOC2, encrypted at rest, KMS integration and VPC isolation are must-haves. Also audit logs and SSO (SAML) for RBAC.
[00:01:02] Maya Chen: That's helpful. One high-level question — are you thinking hosted first and then maybe dedicated, or private on day one?
[00:01:09] Priya Nair: We'd like to pilot hosted to move fast, but need a path to dedicated or private in a quarter. Our customers demand more control over keys and maybe data residency for EU accounts.
[00:01:20] Maya Chen: Makes sense. Typical path we see. Diego, do you want to take us through compatibility concerns?
[00:01:24] Diego Alvarez: Sure. You mentioned TGI/vLLM — are you currently self-hosting inference with vLLM for generation and TGI fine-tuned stacks?
[00:01:33] Ethan Wu: Yeah, we run vLLM for low-latency chat on A100s and TGI for some of our tuned models. We also have quantized variants (int8) in prod for cost control.
[00:01:42] Diego Alvarez: Okay. Two main areas: model format and runtime features. Redwood supports common ONNX/pt/ggml flows, and we do kernel selection + quantization-aware paths. For the TGI models, we typically can ingest the weights and keep parity, but sometimes tokenization and padding configs cause small diffs.
[00:02:01] Priya Nair: Padding diffs have bitten us before — small score changes cascade in reranking. How do you validate parity?
[00:02:07] Diego Alvarez: We recommend a parity eval — we can run a benchmark harness against your prompt set, compare outputs at top-k and BLEU-ish metrics, and then do a token-level diff. We'll share the harness.
[00:02:17] Maya Chen: Also note Redwood Optimize has quantization suggestions and we can show unit-cost comparisons for int8 vs fp16 in dedicated pools.
[00:02:26] Liam (Product): For streaming chat, we need sub-200ms first-byte for interactive features. OpenAI meets that now; can Redwood do the same on hosted?
[00:02:35] Diego Alvarez: Hosted usually gets close; depends on region and model. For strict SLOs we'd recommend Dedicated with reserved GPUs or a Private deployment in your VPC. With Dedicated and Smart Routing you can pin a low-latency pool.
[00:02:44] Ethan Wu: Cost — how big a delta between hosted and dedicated? If we reserve, can we get predictable unit pricing?
[00:02:51] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated is reserved capacity with commit pricing; unit cost is lower and latency more predictable. Hosted is pay-as-you-go and great for pilot. We'll send a breakout.
[00:03:05] Priya Nair: On encryption — can customers manage keys? We need HSM/KMS for EU data.
[00:03:10] Diego Alvarez: Private deployments let you bring your own KMS and hold keys behind your VPC. Dedicated has options for customer-managed keys in some contracts. Hosted supports Redwood KMS with envelope encryption but we can discuss enterprise KMS integrations.
[00:03:24] Unidentified (Ops): Our devs sometimes hit tokenization mismatch because of tokenizer versions; does Redwood have a tokenizer compatibility guide?
[00:03:30] Diego Alvarez: We maintain a model catalog with tokenizers, and in the onboarding we'll map tokenizer versions. But yes, some custom TGI forks need minor fixes. That's where the benchmark harness helps identify differences early.
[00:03:44] [00:03:44] Priya Nair: Great, can you walk through a proposed migration plan at high level?
[00:03:49] Maya Chen: Sure — stage 1 pilot on Hosted using a small fraction of traffic and your sample prompt set. Run parity tests against vLLM/TGI outputs. Stage 2 deploy Dedicated for production features needing low latency and predictable cost. Stage 3, if you need full control or EU residency, deploy Private (VPC/on-prem) with BYOK and audit logging.
[00:04:10] Ethan Wu: How long does Stage 1 typically take?
[00:04:14] Maya Chen: Pilot often runs 2–4 weeks for parity + perf checks. Benchmarks + sample data first week, iterative fixes second.
[00:04:21] Sara Bloom: We'll need an NDA before sharing logs. Also require ISO / SOC docs before prod.
[00:04:27] Maya Chen: No problem. We'll send SOC2 docs and PII handling overview in the follow-up.
[00:04:32] Liam (Product): Regarding reranking — we rely on deterministic outputs for A/B tests. Any non-determinism from beam search or sampling differences to watch for?
[00:04:40] Diego Alvarez: Determinism depends on sampling seeds and kernel implementations. We can configure deterministic generation modes and align sampling parameters. But if you use top-k with different tokenizers, some drift is expected.
[00:04:53] Ethan Wu: For embeddings — our index size is ~3M vectors, we reindex weekly. Do you have throughput guidance for large-batch embedding sends?
[00:05:02] Diego Alvarez: We have batching recommendations and a dedicated embedding pipeline. For large indexing, offload to a burst pool or asynchronous jobs; we'll provide throughput numbers per model/instance type.
[00:05:12] Priya Nair: A few nitty-gritty infra questions — Do you support egress controls, private endpoints, and peering?
[00:05:19] Diego Alvarez: For Private yes; Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints in some regions. Hosted has IP allowlists and regional routing, but not full VPC peering.
[00:05:29] Unidentified (Ops): Any notes about KV cache behavior — we use KV cache extensively for chat context in vLLM, how do you treat that?
[00:05:36] Diego Alvarez: Redwood uses KV cache management in the runtime and supports prefix / KV caching and reuse to reduce token costs. We expose hooks to manage cache invalidation per session. Sometimes transcriptions show 'k-v cash' but that's the same.
[00:05:48] [00:06:00] Priya Nair: Can you talk about fallbacks — if a model is down or capacity constrained?
[00:06:06] Maya Chen: Smart routing can fall back to compatible model variants — e.g., larger fp16 variant to smaller int8 variant, or different region. Also we can set automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated capacity is temporarily saturated.
[00:06:19] Ethan Wu: Any customer references doing a similar OpenAI exit?
[00:06:23] Maya Chen: Yes — we have examples in analytics and fintech that moved from OpenAI to a mix of hosted+dedi. We'll include a short list and anonymized latency/cost case studies.
[00:06:31] [00:06:45] Liam (Product): On the evaluation side — can you run automated regression alerts against our prompt sets?
[00:06:51] Diego Alvarez: Redwood Optimize does quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals. We'll show how thresholds map to alerts and rollbacks.
[00:07:01] Priya Nair: If we find parity gaps, is rollback automatic? We need automatic fallback while we iterate on models.
[00:07:06] Maya Chen: We can configure A/B rollouts and automatic fallback policies. If the new model fails quality checks, traffic can revert to previous model version.
[00:07:15] [00:07:30] Sara Bloom: A security question — can Redwood provide signed audit logs and retention controls? We have long retention needs for some markets.
[00:07:36] Diego Alvarez: Yes, audit trails, signed logs, and retention configs are available especially for dedicated/private customers. We'll align on retention period in contract.
[00:07:47] Priya Nair: Let's talk numbers — our peak is ~180 QPS on short chat endpoints, average token length ~60, 70% reads, 30% writes. We need p95 below 300ms for the majority of these. Cost sensitivity is medium-high.
[00:08:02] Diego Alvarez: That QPS is well within Dedicated pool sizing; for Hosted we'd estimate a modest delta in p95, but Dedicated gives more predictability. We'll model cost per 1M tokens and also show reserved pricing scenarios.
[00:08:13] Ethan Wu: Any differences in appliance for TGI vs vLLM models when ingested? We saw latencies increase for TGI converted models in other infra.
[00:08:22] Diego Alvarez: Sometimes TGI-specific kernels or padding cause overhead; we profile and choose kernels or reorder attention to match performance. Part of the benchmark is to surface those hotspots.
[00:08:34] [00:08:45] Priya Nair: For the pilot, what do you need from us?
[00:08:49] Maya Chen: Sample prompt set, 7-day traffic traces (anonymized), a list of models and tokenizers, and an NDA for full logs. We'll send an onboarding checklist.
[00:09:00] Liam (Product): On instrumentation — can we get request-level tracing into our APM (Datadog)?
[00:09:06] Diego Alvarez: Yes, Redwood Console exposes traces and we can send spans to your APM with integrations. We can also add custom tags for request IDs.
[00:09:16] Sara Bloom: Do you support per-route RBAC and token scoping?
[00:09:21] Maya Chen: Yes — RBAC with token scoping, per-route policies, and quotas are part of the Console. We'll show screenshots in the follow-up.
[00:09:29] [00:09:45] Unidentified (Ops): Does Redwood publish model performance profiles so we can pre-approx costs?
[00:09:51] Diego Alvarez: We publish curated performance profiles in the model catalog, including latency and throughput numbers per hardware type. For custom models we'll run quick profiling.
[00:10:03] [00:10:20] Priya Nair: Quick tangent — we have regulatory constraints for EU customers: data residency and logs within EU. How does Redwood address that?
[00:10:27] Diego Alvarez: Private deployments in EU regions are available; Dedicated can be provisioned in region with contractual controls. We'll surface options.
[00:10:36] Ethan Wu: For the parity harness — can it compare embeddings drift as well as generation drift?
[00:10:42] Diego Alvarez: Yes, the harness will compare embeddings similarities (cosine) and track drift thresholds, plus reranker score deltas.
[00:10:52] [00:11:10] Priya Nair: Let's talk SLAs — what do you offer for Dedicated?
[00:11:15] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with uptime SLA and latency targets in the contract. We'll include specific SLO wording in the commercial packet.
[00:11:24] Liam (Product): Any gotchas with client SDKs? We use a mix of Python and Node.
[00:11:29] Diego Alvarez: SDKs for Python/Node are available; we also have a REST API. Occasionally customers hit small versioning differences in streaming APIs; we keep backward compat.
[00:11:41] [00:11:55] Priya Nair: One last technical: are you able to support model weights that use custom attention modifications?
[00:12:01] Diego Alvarez: Custom attention sometimes requires small runtime patches — doable but we'll need access to model code and tests. That's usually a SE-led project.
[00:12:10] Maya Chen: Ok, quick recap of next steps — we'll send pricing, SOC2 docs, parity harness, and the onboarding checklist. Aerolith will share prompt set and traces. Then we schedule a deeper technical session focusing on parity and dedicated sizing.
[00:12:24] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Also please include references of customers who did OpenAI exits if possible.
[00:12:29] Maya Chen: Will do.
[00:12:32] [00:12:40] (crosstalk) Ethan Wu: Thanks all.
[00:12:44] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the deck.

--- End transcript excerpt (first 13 minutes shown; call continued with Q&A and detailed infra questions, bench notes and scheduling) ---
